verdict: Paid lead count dropped sharply, but an attribution gap explains most of it.
narrative: In the last 28 days, your paid channels recorded 30 leads at a cost per lead of $43.77 — a steep rise from the prior week driven largely by a tracking gap, not a collapse in customer demand. Your CRM shows 87 won opportunities this period, a figure that cannot yet be reconciled with the 30 leads the ad platforms are reporting; the discrepancy is being investigated and conversion tracking is being repaired so this number under-reports true volume. At the same time, your Google Business Profile activity surged — 186 actions including 21 calls and 140 direction requests — signaling that organic demand is growing even while paid signals went quiet. A confirmed three-day stretch at the end of October produced zero paid leads, which is being addressed through a creative and campaign review now underway. Once tracking is restored, expect the reported cost per lead to correct downward and scale decisions to move forward.

highlights.phrase: opportunities won in your CRM this period, against 30 leads recorded by ad platforms — the gap is a tracking issue, not lost business
Google Business Profile actions (calls, direction requests, website clicks) this period, up sharply from the prior week
cost per lead as reported this period — expected to correct downward once conversion tracking is repaired

watch_item.issue: A confirmed three-day lead drought (Oct 30–Nov 1) coincides with a broken conversion tracking connection that is making paid results look worse than they are.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being repaired this week and ad creative is under review; results will be reassessed once clean data is flowing.
